study.status: confirmatory supplement to Fleet C1 (PDR-0057 G1 deficit screen); owner chose 'Supplement after fleet' in session, 2026-10-10
study.question: On the BatchNorm hosts, does static, born at tau, beat no-growth by more than 0.05 nats with the 95% lower bound above 0, without diverging in more than 10% of units? This is PDR-0057's deficit screen, unchanged; only the static arm is corrected.

disclosures: Why: Fleet C1's registered static arm calibrates tau on eval-mode host features, so on BatchNorm hosts it is born at about 1/30 of tau (simic-e3803e8200). The Fleet C1 pilot's birth witnesses show realised ratios of 0.0013-0.0018 against 0.05 on these three hosts, and 0.0500 on under_normalized.

Seen before this plan: the pilot's late-CE differences, static (or graft) minus no-growth, n=24, no reading, all from the defective static arm. Positive means worse than no-growth; the screen's static_gain has the opposite sign. Static: channel_starved +0.002, mild +0.017, no_spatial_mix -0.005. Graft: -0.008, -0.001, -0.022.

The arm: experiments.atlas.Unit.static(seed_type, calibration='train') -> experiments.atlas_static.attach_static_train_calibrated. Tau is read in train mode under no_grad, and every host buffer, module mode and hook statistic is restored. The frozen runner is unchanged.
A 30x larger birth may make static diverge more often (simic-9c5c3a2acf). The divergence rate is a result, guarded by the parent's static_divergence_cap.

Not a prediction: the pilot's defective static gain grew within the first epoch on channel_starved (median 0.12 at epoch 0's end), so the correction may change late CE little there; mild's gain stayed small.
No Fleet C1 unit output was opened before this plan or its revision; only its progress log (seed, GPU, return code, wall time) and launch records were read.

Order (statistics review): Fleet C1-S launches when Fleet C1 finishes and before Fleet C1's own analysis; a fresh launch is refused once Fleet C1's report exists. Every module the arm and the reading run through is pinned in source_sha256 and checked at launch and analysis.

Every seed, not only the 48 pairing seeds: the corrected arm's birth hashes that do not depend on the calibration mode (host and seed-body init, calibration inputs, optimizer) and the unit's future and data must equal Fleet C1's; each corrected arm must be born within 5% of tau. A mismatch is a pairing_failure; an arm not born at tau fails its seed's verification, so all three of that seed's units count as failed (as Fleet C1 treats any malformed row).
Fleet C1-S makes no reading if Fleet C1's own instrument is not ok.

Reported beside the screen, descriptive: the gain over completed runs only (so 'failed by instability' is told apart from 'no deficit'; each divergence moves the mean by about 1/n nats) and corrected minus registered static.
max_failed_units 22: the parent's rate (30 of 3,072 units) applied to this fleet's 2,304 (768 seeds x 3 hosts). A seed whose parent unit fails verification counts here too.

Pairing: on seeds 10001-10048 the unit also re-trains no-growth on the three hosts, and static_calibrated on under_normalized. Both must equal Fleet C1's records bit for bit, or there is no reading. The control host's screen is Fleet C1's own.
fallback: If Fleet C1-S makes no reading (parent_failure, pairing_failure or instrument_failure), the BatchNorm hosts are unscreened: Fleet C1's registered screen on them never enters Fleet A, and John decides. Any re-run is a new plan that lists its deviations.
